report.headline: Transient burst across subsystem metrics m09, m14, and m01 lasting 11 minutes on machine-1-1.
report.summary: An 11-minute multi-metric anomaly triggered alarms across 9 of 10 detectors starting at minute 15847. Initial spikes in metrics m09, m14, m13, and m15 immediately triggered the incident, followed at minute 2 by a sustained elevation in m01. The pattern resolved automatically after 11 minutes but recurred in longer subsequent incidents.
report.likely_cause: Transient subsystem overload or burst batch job driving high localized activity in m09/m14, inducing follow-on load on m01.
timeline: Minute 0 (15847): Simultaneous sharp spikes in first-movers m09, m13, m14, and m15 trigger alarms across 7 detectors at 100% window coverage.
Minute 2 (15849): Metric m01 crosses 3 SD, shifting from baseline mean 0.0642 to an incident mean of 0.3998.
Minutes 3-10 (15850-15857): High correlated co-movement across group [m01, m09, m12, m13, m14, m15] peaks with m09 reaching peak_abs_z of 31.39.
Minute 11 (15858): All metrics drop back below threshold and alarms clear.
evidence: m09 surged to an extreme peak_abs_z of 31.39 and incident peak of 0.3342 versus baseline mean of 0.0203.
m01 exhibited a sustained surge with mean z_score of 5.92 and incident peak of 0.4946 (baseline 0.0642).
m14 spiked instantly at minute 0 with peak_abs_z of 22.89 and peak value of 0.4086.
Strong detector consensus with 9/10 models alarming and 7 maintaining 100% window detection.
investigation_steps: Run 'journalctl --since "15847 minutes ago" -n 200' to identify scheduled tasks, cron triggers, or service restarts coinciding with the window.
Inspect historical sar/sysstat CPU and memory accounting using 'sar -u -f /var/log/sa/saXX' and 'sar -r -f /var/log/sa/saXX' around the incident window.
Check disk and block device load history using 'sar -d -f /var/log/sa/saXX' to verify if m09/m14 correlate with I/O bursts.
Check kernel ring buffer using 'dmesg -T' for driver warnings, memory throttling, or hardware stalls during the timestamp range.
report.caveats: Because metrics m01-m38 are anonymized, exact physical resources (CPU, memory, disk, network) cannot be definitively separated without correlating to host-level logs.
